title: 5 ways Amazon is investing in Missouri
summary: Amazon has invested more than $9 billion in Missouri since 2010, creating 10,000+ jobs and supporting local businesses and communities across the state.
body_markdown:
---


## Key takeaways


- Amazon has


[invested more than $9 billion in Missouri](https://assets.aboutamazon.com/dc/c1/4ce725474e9d842c2ed83aaa0a53/amazoninvestment-missouri-2025.pdf) since 2010 and contributed over $9 billion to the state's economy.


- The company has more than 10,000 full- and part-time employees and supports more than 10,000 indirect jobs.


- Amazon partners with seven educational institutions in Missouri through its


[Career Choice program](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/career-choice) and has upskilled over 1,000 employees since 2019.


- Missouri-based independent sellers sold more than 43 million items through Amazon's store.


---


For more than 30 years, Amazon has been investing across the United States, strengthening local economies and creating opportunities for communities nationwide. Missouri is a prime example of this commitment, with Amazon building a substantial presence in the state since 2017.


An Amazon team member loads boxes in at Missouri fulfillment center, SMO1.


Today, Missouri serves as a thriving innovation and logistics hub for Amazon, with investments spanning


[fulfillment centers](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/fulfillment-center) to


[Whole Foods Market locations](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/tag/whole-foods-market) . The company's economic impact extends beyond direct employment, supporting thousands of additional jobs in construction, logistics, and professional services, and helping local businesses reach customers around the world.


Here are five ways Amazon is investing in Missouri:


## 1. Investing in our employees


Amazon provides


[competitive wages and comprehensive benefits](https://www.aboutamazon.com/workplace/employee-benefits) from Day 1. Core operations employees in customer fulfillment and transportation earn an average hourly base wage of more than $24, with total compensation averaging more than $32 an hour when including benefits. These benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance starting on Day 1, free mental health resources, up to 20 weeks of fully paid parental leave, a 401(k) with 50% company match,


[a grocery discount](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-us-employee-grocery-discount)[a grocery discount](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-us-employee-grocery-discount) , and flexible time-off options that increase with tenure.


[Amazon raises minimum starting pay for full-time core operations employees to $20/hour, with average pay reaching nearly $24/hour](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-raises-minimum-starting-pay-adds-grocery-banking-benefits)


Amazon invests more than $1.5 billion in higher pay for U.S. core operations employees, alongside new benefits designed to help our teammates’ money go further.


Beyond more than 10,000 direct jobs, Amazon's presence in Missouri supports more than 10,000 indirect jobs in industries such as construction, logistics, and professional services—suppliers and partners whom we rely on every day.


## 2. Investing in workforce development and upskilling


Amazon is committed to preparing its workforce for future opportunities through comprehensive education and


[skills training programs](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/amazon-ai-courses-certifications-aws-trainings) . Since 2019, more than 1,000 Missouri employees have participated in these free initiatives.


In Missouri, Amazon partners with seven educational institutions through its


[Career Choice](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/career-choice-free-education-for-amazon-employees) program, which prepays tuition for employees pursuing further education. These partnerships with colleges and universities across the state help Amazon employees gain in-demand skills that can propel them into new careers. From Machine Learning University to Career Choice, these programs represent Amazon's investment in developing talent and creating pathways to opportunity for its workforce.


[Amazon commits $1 billion to Career Choice employee education program as part of Future Ready 2030 fund](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/workplace/amazon-future-of-work-skills-jobs-training)


The Future Ready 2030 fund supports students, employees, and those looking to expand their skills as the workforce adapts to a changing economy.


## 3. Building infrastructure across the Show Me State


Since 2010, Amazon has invested over $9 billion in Missouri's infrastructure and employee compensation, contributing more than $9 billion to the state's gross domestic product.


An Amazon team member moves stock through SMO1, a same-day delivery fulfillment center in Missouri


These investments include seven fulfillment and sortation centers, six delivery stations, four rural super rural delivery stations, and other facilities across the state. The company has also expanded its retail footprint with four Whole Foods Market locations across Missouri. Amazon continues to grow its


[sustainable infrastructure](https://www.aboutamazon.com/planet/sustainable-operations) as well, with a solar farm in the state.


[Amazon brings its first renewable energy projects to Missouri](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/sustainability/amazon-extends-position-as-worlds-largest-corporate-buyer-of-renewable-energy)


The company announces 37 new renewable energy projects totaling 3.5 GW of clean energy capacity.


## 4. Empowering Missouri's small businesses


Amazon provides a powerful opportunity for Missouri's entrepreneurs and small businesses to reach customers worldwide. Missouri-based independent sellers—primarily small and medium-sized businesses—sold more than 43 million items through Amazon's store, with the average seller generating more than $310,000 in annual sales.


[Tummy Drops](https://sellingpartners.aboutamazon.com/two-missouri-doctors-scale-a-business-they-built-between-patient-appointments-with-help-from-amazons-seller-tools)


co-founders Dustin and Helen James in their kitchen with bags of their organic lozenges, which they developed after patients kept asking for natural digestive remedies.


These independent sellers represent more than 60% of sales in Amazon's store. Their success contributes significantly to local economies, with more than 65% of U.S. independent sellers employing at least one person within 50 miles of their primary business location.


By providing infrastructure, logistics support, and access to millions of customers, Amazon enables Missouri's small businesses to scale their operations and create additional jobs throughout the state.


## 5. Investing as a good neighbor


[Amazon strengthens its investment in Missouri to bring new community programs, new jobs, and hundreds of millions in tax revenue](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/company-news/amazon-data-center-missouri-new-jobs)


New commitments include funding for emergency services, a water stewardship project, and a new community gathering space enabled by data center investments.


Amazon uses its global scale and strengths to make a positive impact in communities. Working with trusted community partners, we address critical needs—food security, education, disaster relief—using our logistics, technology, and innovation, while investing as a good neighbor in the communities where our employees live and work.


Amazon employees from Missouri's STL8 facility volunteer at a community event supporting cancer awareness in March 2023.


Amazon has delivered more than 300,000 meals on behalf of food banks and nonprofits across the state. The company has reached more than 10,000 students and 1,000 teachers through education programs and supported more than 100,000 computer science learning hours. More than 700 Amazon employees have volunteered in communities across Missouri.

[investing in Missouri](https://www.aboutamazon.com/impact/amazon-missouri) and the
